points.title: 音乐启蒙
points.description: 巴赫出生于德国艾森纳赫的一个音乐世家，他的家族几代人都以音乐为生。父亲是镇上的小提琴手和管风琴师，叔父们也都是杰出的音乐家。巴赫从小就展现出非凡的音乐天赋，在父亲和叔父们的指导下学习小提琴、管风琴和古钢琴。1695年父母双亡后，他前往奥尔德鲁夫与长兄同住，继续接受音乐教育。这段早期经历为巴赫奠定了坚实的音乐基础，培养了他对复调音乐的深刻理解。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Eisenach into a family of musicians, Bach showed exceptional musical talent from a young age. His father was a violinist and organist, and his uncles were prominent musicians. Under their guidance, Bach learned violin, organ, and harpsichord. After his parents' death in 1695, he moved to Ohrdruf to live with his eldest brother, continuing his musical education. These early years laid a solid foundation for Bach, developing his deep understanding of polyphonic music.

points.title: 宫廷乐手
points.description: 1703年，巴赫成为魏玛宫廷小提琴手，随后转任阿恩施塔特新教堂的管风琴师。在阿恩施塔特期间，他因音乐风格与教会当局产生分歧，特别是他即兴演奏的复杂复调音乐被认为过于华丽而受到批评。1705年，他徒步前往吕贝克聆听著名管风琴家布克斯特胡德的演奏，并停留了四个月，这极大地影响了他的创作风格。这段经历也导致他返回阿恩施塔特时因长期缺勤而受到教会纪律处分，最终促使他于1707年接受米尔豪森圣布拉修斯教堂的管风琴师职位。
points.descriptionEn: In 1703, Bach became a violinist at the Weimar court, then moved to Arnstadt as organist at the New Church. During this period, he clashed with church authorities over his complex polyphonic improvisations, which they considered too ornate. In 1705, he walked to Lübeck to hear the renowned organist Buxtehude, staying for four months, which profoundly influenced his compositional style. This extended absence led to disciplinary action from the church, eventually prompting Bach to accept the position of organist at St. Blasius Church in Mühlhausen in 1707.

points.title: 宫廷乐长
points.description: 巴赫重返魏玛，这次被任命为宫廷乐长和管风琴师。这一时期是他创作管风琴作品的黄金阶段，创作了著名的《d小调托卡塔与赋格》、《c小调帕萨卡利亚》等杰作。同时，他开始创作大量康塔塔，为魏玛宫廷礼拜服务。1713年，巴赫申请接受卡塞尔宫廷乐长职位未果，反而获得了魏玛宫廷副乐长的头衔。这一时期巴赫的声望日益增长，但也因与魏玛公爵的关系紧张，特别是当他申请接受克滕宫廷乐长职位时，公爵甚至将他短暂监禁。这段经历促使巴赫最终于1717年离开魏玛，前往克滕。
points.descriptionEn: Returning to Weimar, Bach was appointed Court Konzertmeister and organist. This period marked his golden age for organ composition, producing masterpieces like the Toccata and Fugue in D minor and the Passacaglia in C minor. He also began composing numerous cantatas for the court services. In 1713, Bach applied for the position of Kapellmeister in Kassel but was unsuccessful, instead receiving the title of Court Konzertmeister in Weimar. His growing prestige led to tensions with the Duke of Weimar, especially when he sought the position of Kapellmeister in Köthen, which resulted in brief imprisonment. This experience prompted Bach to leave Weimar for Köthen in 1717.

points.title: 世俗音乐巅峰
points.description: 巴赫在克滕担任安哈尔特-克滕亲王的乐长，这是他职业生涯中唯一一个专注于世俗音乐的时期。由于亲王是新教改革派，不重视教堂音乐，巴赫得以专注于器乐创作。这一时期他创作了著名的《勃兰登堡协奏曲》、《无伴奏大提琴组曲》、《无伴奏小提琴奏鸣曲与组曲》以及《平均律钢琴曲集》第一卷。1720年，巴赫的妻子芭芭拉去世，这给他带来了巨大打击。1721年，他与安娜·玛格达莱娜·威廉结婚，她是一位出色的歌手和音乐抄写员，对巴赫的后期作品整理和保存做出了重要贡献。1723年，巴赫接受了莱比锡圣托马斯教堂乐长的职位，结束了他在克滕的时期。
points.descriptionEn: In Köthen, Bach served as Kapellmeister to Prince Leopold of Anhalt-Köthen, the only period in his career focused solely on secular music. As the prince was a Calvinist who didn't value church music, Bach could concentrate on instrumental compositions. During this time, he created the Brandenburg Concertos, Cello Suites, Sonatas and Partitas for Solo Violin, and the first book of The Well-Tempered Clavier. In 1720, Bach's first wife Barbara died, causing him great grief. In 1721, he married Anna Magdalena Wilcke, an accomplished singer and music copyist who played a crucial role in preserving and organizing his later works. In 1723, Bach accepted the position of Thomaskantor in Leipzig, ending his time in Köthen.

points.title: 教堂音乐大师
points.description: 巴赫在莱比锡担任圣托马斯教堂乐长，负责管理莱比锡的四座主要教堂的音乐事务。这一时期是他创作康塔塔最丰富的阶段，每周创作一首康塔塔，共创作了约200首。他还创作了《马太受难曲》、《b小调弥撒》等大型宗教作品。1730年代，巴赫与莱比锡市政当局的关系日益紧张，特别是在学校管理和音乐资源分配方面。尽管如此，他的声望依然不断增长，1747年他被普鲁士国王腓特烈二世邀请到波茨坦宫廷，即兴演奏了国王的主题，后来将其发展为《音乐的奉献》。巴赫晚年视力逐渐衰退，1750年因眼部手术并发症去世，享年65岁。他被安葬于莱比锡圣约翰教堂，后遗体迁至圣托马斯教堂。
points.descriptionEn: In Leipzig, Bach served as Thomaskantor, responsible for music at the city's four main churches. This period was his most prolific for cantata composition, with approximately 200 works written, one for each Sunday. He also created major religious works like the St. Matthew Passion and the Mass in B minor. In the 1730s, Bach's relationship with Leipzig authorities deteriorated, particularly regarding school management and music resources. Despite these tensions, his reputation continued to grow. In 1747, he was invited to the court of Frederick the Great in Potsdam, where he improvised on a royal theme, later developed into The Musical Offering. Bach's vision gradually declined in his later years, and he died in 1750 at age 65 from complications following eye surgery. He was initially buried at St. John's Church in Leipzig, later reinterred at St. Thomas's Church.

supporter.zh: 巴赫被誉为西方音乐史上最伟大的作曲家之一，他的作品代表了巴洛克音乐的巅峰。支持者认为巴赫通过严谨的复调技巧和深刻的宗教情感，将音乐提升到了前所未有的艺术高度。他的《平均律钢琴曲集》被音乐理论家视为音乐圣经，而他的宗教作品则展现了信仰与艺术的完美结合。巴赫的音乐遗产对后世作曲家产生了深远影响，从莫扎特、贝多芬到现代作曲家，都从他作品中汲取灵感。他被视为音乐史上最伟大的复调大师，其作品结构之严谨、情感之丰富至今仍令人叹为观止。
supporter.en: Bach is regarded as one of the greatest composers in Western music history, with his works representing the pinnacle of Baroque music. Supporters argue that through rigorous contrapuntal techniques and profound religious emotion, Bach elevated music to unprecedented artistic heights. His Well-Tempered Clavier is considered a musical bible by theorists, while his religious works demonstrate the perfect fusion of faith and art. Bach's legacy has profoundly influenced later composers, from Mozart and Beethoven to modern composers, all drawing inspiration from his works. He is seen as the greatest master of counterpoint in musical history, whose works' structural rigor and emotional richness continue to inspire awe.

critic.zh: 批评者指出巴赫的作品过于复杂和学术化，缺乏情感的自然流露。一些评论家认为他的音乐过于注重形式而忽视了听众的接受度，特别是在他生前，他的作品并未获得广泛认可。巴赫在职业生涯中也面临多次争议，包括与教会和雇主的冲突，以及被指控在克滕期间未能充分履行职务。此外，巴赫在音乐创新方面相对保守，他很少采用当时新兴的意大利风格，而是坚持传统的德国复调传统。这些批评者认为，巴赫的声誉很大程度上是19世纪浪漫主义时期音乐家们重新发现和推崇的结果，而非他生前实际获得的认可。
critic.en: Critics point out that Bach's works are overly complex and academic, lacking natural emotional expression. Some argue that his music emphasizes form at the expense of audience accessibility, as his works were not widely recognized during his lifetime. Bach also faced several controversies in his career, including conflicts with churches and employers, and accusations of failing to fulfill his duties adequately in Köthen. Additionally, Bach was relatively conservative in musical innovation, rarely adopting the emerging Italian styles while adhering to traditional German contrapuntal traditions. These critics suggest that Bach's reputation was largely the result of 19th-century Romantic musicians rediscovering and promoting his works, rather than the recognition he actually received during his lifetime.

objective.zh: 从历史学和流行文化视角看，巴赫被定义为连接巴洛克与古典时期的关键桥梁。他的作品既保留了巴洛克时期的复杂性和装饰性，又预示了古典时期的清晰结构和情感表达。在学术界，巴赫被视为音乐史上最重要的复调大师，他的作品被广泛研究和分析。在流行文化中，巴赫的形象经历了从被遗忘到被神化的转变过程。20世纪以来，他的作品被广泛应用于电影、广告和流行音乐中，如《G弦上的咏叹调》已成为全球最著名的古典音乐片段之一。巴赫被符号化为音乐天才的典范，代表着德国文化的精髓和西方音乐的最高成就。
objective.en: From historical and cultural perspectives, Bach is defined as a crucial bridge between the Baroque and Classical periods. His works preserved the complexity and ornamentation of the Baroque era while anticipating the clear structure and emotional expression of the Classical period. Academically, Bach is regarded as the most important master of counterpoint in musical history, with his works extensively studied and analyzed. In popular culture, Bach's image has transformed from being largely forgotten to being deified. Since the 20th century, his works have been widely used in films, advertisements, and popular music, with the Air on the G String becoming one of the most recognizable classical music excerpts globally. Bach has been symbolized as the archetype of musical genius, representing the essence of German culture and the pinnacle of Western music.

self.zh: 音乐始于上帝的沉默，终于人类的祈祷。

others.zh: 巴赫的音乐不是为我们的耳朵，而是为上帝的耳朵而创作的。
others.en: Bach's music was not written for our ears, but for the ears of God.
